title: Fomo Kernel Trade Evaluation
description: One row per `review.py consider` call (docs/decision-fomo-kernel-shape.md Layer 2): a user mid-decision asks what a hypothetical trade does to their book, away from any review session. The readable contract; skills/fomo-kernel/engine/review.py's cmd_consider holds the enforcement, because the offline suite carries no jsonschema dependency. Stored in <root>/trade_evaluations.jsonl, append-only. Every field is a frozen value computed at the time of the ask, never a pointer into mutable state -- the ledger keeps growing after this row is written, and a later reconciliation must see what the engine actually said then, not what it would say now (the frozen-subject design ratified in issue #446's specification comment). A resolution (`--resolve`) appends a new row carrying the same evaluation_id rather than rewriting this one; the fold picks whichever row for that id appears last in the file.

evaluation_id.description: Engine-assigned, content-addressed identity (eval-<hash of premise+basis+created+consequence+rule_collisions, plus context when one was supplied>), the same convention session.py uses for snapshot_id/adjustment_id/reconciliation_id. Asking the identical premise again the same day against an unchanged book converges on the same id rather than minting a new one; asking it with a different stated why_now does not, because that is a different question about the same trade (issue #479). See review.py's _evaluation_id for why the seed carries the frozen result rather than an enumerated list of the inputs that produced it.

created.description: The date this evaluation was asked (today, at CLI invocation time) -- distinct from premise.date, which is when the hypothetical trade itself would happen.

premise.description: The normalized hypothetical trade consequence.validate_premise() returned: ticker, side, qty, price, date, currency. notional, when the caller supplied it, is already consumed into qty by validation time and never appears here.

context.description: The user's own reason, why-now and evidence references at the moment of the ask (issue #479), when the caller supplied them through --decision-context. The shape is declared once, in decision-context.schema.json, and $ref-ed here rather than restated -- the same treatment `premise` gets above. Absent, never null, on a call that carried no context: this property's presence is exactly the condition review.py's _evaluation_id uses to decide whether the context enters the identity seed, so a row without the key and a seed without the key are the same fact read twice. Frozen like every other field here -- a --resolve appends a new row carrying this context unchanged, and nothing rewrites, translates or re-derives the user's words afterwards.

basis.description: Frozen evaluation footing. Ledger-backed current-book evaluations carry PortfolioBasis identity/disclosures so a later reader can see exactly what holdings fact answered; explicit CSV input remains the separate historical FIFO compatibility lane and declares itself unverified rather than impersonating a reconciled current book.

source.description: PortfolioBasis source for ledger-backed current-book evaluation; transactions denotes the separate explicit CSV/FIFO compatibility lane.

as_of.description: The date of the record's own latest row -- the last trade or snapshot anchor the reconstructed book actually reflects.

stale_days.description: created minus as_of, in days. Disclosed, never gated on -- issue #456 leaves the question of an interruption-worthy threshold explicitly unresolved; a large value means the answer is confidently computed on a record that may no longer match the real book, not that the answer was refused.

completeness.description: How the frozen current-book source was obtained: declared_complete when a recorded book row anchored it, unverified when the book came from transaction replay alone. Disclosed, never gated on -- #485 removed the completeness gates and #549 removed the completeness flag itself. declared_partial is retained for replay compatibility only: no engine path can produce it since #549, and a stored row carrying it predates that change.

cost_basis.description: Cost convention used by the frozen basis. fifo exists only for explicit CSV compatibility; canonical PortfolioBasis uses the other values.

valuation_basis.description: Whether the current-book basis carried a supplied valuation manifest. An unpriced consequence remains a disclosed cost-basis computation, not a zero-price valuation.

reconciliation_ref.description: The selected canonical snapshot anchor, if one exists.

state_version.description: Deterministic basis identity. PortfolioBasis uses pb-v1:<sha256>; CSV compatibility uses its own csv-v1:<sha256> identity and is not a current-book reconciliation version.

valuation_coverage.description: Canonical sizing projection coverage for a ledger-backed current-book evaluation. This makes mixed price/cost fallback visible; absent on the separate CSV compatibility lane.

as_of.description: The newest per-ticker observation this answer actually used -- max(by_ticker), computed from the map below rather than copied from the price envelope's own declared as_of. The envelope's frame date is an upper bound price_feed.parse enforces on its rows, not an observation: a supplied envelope may declare today while every close in it is yesterday's, and copying it forward would put the summary ahead of every number it summarizes. market_data.to_price_feed_envelope already defines its own as_of as max(row date) for the same reason.

by_ticker.description: Per instrument, the market session its close was observed on -- price_feed.parse's own observed_date, never re-derived. Per ticker rather than one frame date because a frame-level as_of cannot say which session a given instrument's number came from, and one fresh instrument then makes every stale one look same-day (#583 section 2). Scoped to what this answer needed priced -- the held book, whatever it could not value, and the premise's own ticker -- the same universe the price_feed recovery kit is built over, so an envelope carrying closes for instruments no number here uses does not date them.

price_observations.description: Which market session each number in this answer was valued at (#618). Absent -- never null, never a placeholder, never today's date -- whenever valuation_basis is unpriced, which is the whole point: a run that priced nothing must not grow a date, and the cost_basis disclosure is what speaks for that answer instead. Frozen beside valuation_basis because that is where the was-this-priced fact already lives. Before #611 a consider weight was a share of cost or of whatever the last review froze, so the same premise re-asked returned the same weights; it is now a share of the current close, and without this the user can see that the numbers moved with no way to tell whether the market moved or their own book did.

consequence.description: The frozen return of engine/consequence.py's consequence(). before/after/delta are not restated field-by-field here -- that shape belongs to consequence.py alone, the same posture session-bundle.schema.json takes toward engine_state/engine_card.

before.description: portfolio_state() over the book alone. See consequence.py for the field contract.

after.description: portfolio_state() over the book plus the hypothetical trade. See consequence.py for the field contract.

delta.description: Signed after-minus-before changes for the readings that moved; a field absent here did not move. See consequence.py's _delta().

excluded_holdings.description: Positions left out of the usable book, and therefore outside the denominator every number above is measured against (#515, #673). Empty when the whole book was usable. The identities live here rather than inside `disclosures`, which is machine-readable keys and never carries data: `partial_book` says THAT something was excluded, this says WHAT. Any consumer stating a derived number must name these alongside it -- a partial denominator that does not say it is partial is worse than the refusal it replaced. Nearly always a currently-held position; an `integrity_*` entry can also name a ticker the book records no position in, because a recorded zero is exactly what an unmatched sell puts in doubt (#673).

reason.description: Why this holding is outside the usable book, mirroring consequence.EXCLUSION_REASONS. Engine-assigned; never a user or agent claim. The first two are facts missing from the holding (#515). `integrity_oversell` is not a missing fact but an underivable one (#673): the ledger recorded a sell with no matching prior buy, so the replay clamped it and this holding's share count is not what the history can account for. That distinction is load-bearing -- a premise about an `integrity_*` holding is refused by name, while a holding with no cost on record is merely outside the denominator.

unclassified_holdings.description: Held positions with no sector/AI classification, and therefore contributing zero to `ai_pct` and dropped from `max_sector_pct`'s numerator entirely (#598). Same division of labour as `excluded_holdings` above: the `unclassified_book` disclosure says THAT the concentration figures were computed over a partially-legible book, this says WHICH positions and at what weight, so an answer can state the size of what it could not read. Absent on rows written before #598; a position below the residual floor (trade_recap.RESIDUAL_POS_TH) is not listed, since it moves no figure and would only buy the answer a sentence about dust.

weight.description: Its weight in the same after-state denominator every other percentage on this row is measured against.

undecomposed_etfs.description: Held fund positions whose constituents nothing in this engine inspects (#599). An allocation kind is exempted from concentration wholesale and a sector/thematic/leveraged kind counts as one opaque ticker; neither contributes the sector or AI exposure it actually holds, so a concentrated semiconductor fund and a broad world index fund of the same size are equally invisible to `ai_pct` and `max_sector_pct`. Disjoint from `unclassified_holdings` by construction: a fund the instrument map does not recognize is not an ETF as far as this engine is concerned and is listed there instead. Absent on rows written before #599.

kind.description: engine/instruments.py's own kind for it. Engine-assigned; never a user or agent claim.

allocation_exempt.description: true when the position was left out of the concentration numerator wholesale rather than counted as one opaque ticker. Both are undecomposed; they are undecomposed in opposite directions, and an answer that says which one happened is saying something different about the same weight.

disclosures.description: Machine-readable limitation keys, mirroring consequence.DISCLOSURES. Locale wording belongs in renderer copy, never here (docs/maintainer-guide.md, "Honesty decisions belong in code"). `mixed_currency_no_fx` is no longer emitted by any code path -- #600 replaced it with a refusal in portfolio_state, because a currency summed at a 1.0 factor does not make the aggregate incomplete, it inverts it -- and survives in this enum only so rows written before that refusal still validate, the same replay-compatibility posture #549's `declared_partial` has.

rule_collisions.description: One row per currently-tracked rule, mirroring engine/consequence.py's rule_collision(). A muted rule is excluded, matching the rotation it opted out of.

text.description: The rule's own text, verbatim, as stored on rules.jsonl.

problem_key.description: null means this rule's metric_key has no mechanical mapping at all -- state is unmapped, never a silent pass.

state.description: Mirrors consequence.COLLISION_STATES. would_breach: this trade is what freshly crosses the line. already_over: the book was already over the line and stays there, with or without this trade being the cause -- never read as this trade breaking the rule. unjudged: a metric this module cannot evaluate from one hypothetical trade (exit_severity, hold_severity). unmapped: problem_key is null. DIAGNOSTIC since #579: this is where the book stands, not what the transaction does. rule_effect below is the transaction's verdict, and no decision-facing surface may substitute this field for it.

worsens.description: Set only when state is already_over: whether this trade moves the relevant reading in the bad direction. null everywhere else -- a boolean that means nothing outside one state is worse than an absent one. NOT a sufficient direction on its own: consequence._worsened is a strict >, so a reading that fell and a reading that did not move are the same false, which is why #579 added rule_effect below rather than a second boolean.

rule_effect.description: What THIS TRANSACTION does to the rule, mirroring consequence.RULE_EFFECTS and derived by consequence.classify_rule_effect from the reading before, the reading after and the line (#579). This is the field every decision-facing consumer reads; `state` above stays the book's absolute position and is never the transaction's verdict. Reading the state as the verdict is what failed owner-live acceptance on 2026-08-02: a sell taking a position from 80% to 75% against a self-authored 20% cap emits already_over + worsens:false, arithmetically correct, and was described back to the user as breaking the rule. OPTIONAL rather than required, and the asymmetry is deliberate: every row this engine writes now carries it, and a row recorded before it existed must still validate and still replay. A reader that finds it absent falls back to state (answer_provenance._LEGACY_COVERED_STATES, evaluation_challenge._LEGACY_SPEAKING_STATES) rather than inventing an effect. A row carrying an effect its own state cannot accompany is rejected by consequence.effect_disagrees_with_state before either field reaches an answer.

limit.description: The line rule_effect was classified against, as a fraction. null for avgdown_count -- whose reading is a count of breaching events attributable to this trade rather than a level -- and for unjudged/unmapped. Present because the correct sentence names the number ('still above your 20% rule') and no other field in this row carries it.

limit_source.description: Whose line `limit` is, mirroring consequence.LIMIT_SOURCES; null exactly when limit is. user_cap only for max_pos_pct when trade_recap.valid_position_cap accepted the user's own override -- every other threshold this engine compares against is a constant it picked, and handing one back as the user's own rule would put a product default under their name.

decision.description: What the user did with this evaluation. open until a --resolve call records one of the other three; never rewritten in place -- --resolve appends a new row with the same evaluation_id.

decided_on.description: The date --resolve recorded a decision (ISO date), or null while decision is open.

agent_case.description: Optional structured case for and against the trade, supplied by the caller through --agent-case and checked by engine/answer_provenance.py::validate_agent_case against this row's own frozen basis/consequence/rule_collisions before the row is ever written (#414, wired in by #479 Wave B). Never required, and never free prose -- owner ruling 2026-07-27: the agent lists the case for and against and does not take a position, so a submission missing either side is refused rather than accepted one-sided. The shape is declared once, in answer-provenance.schema.json, and $ref-ed here rather than restated -- the same treatment `premise` and `context` get above. That file's own description explains why the shape could not stay this schema's own additionalProperties:false claim $defs: which fields a claim may carry (`anchor`/`worsens`, or `source`/`as_of`) depends on its provenance, and reconciling the two was Wave B's integration decision.
